sources.cite: Microsoft Learn, 'Multi-user authorization using Resource Guard' (Azure Backup), last updated 2026-10-09
sources.note: Relevant text: MUA 'add[s] a layer of protection to critical operations on your Recovery Services vaults and Backup vaults', using 'another Azure resource called Resource Guard'; critical operations include 'Disable soft delete or security features', 'Remove MUA protection' and 'Modify policy' to 'reduce retention'; 'you can place Resource Guard in a subscription or tenant that's different from the one that contains the vaults', and the backup admin 'must not have Contributor, Backup MUA Admin, or Backup MUA Operator permissions' on it. Read through a summarizing fetch on 2026-11-14.

sources.cite: Microsoft Learn, 'Secure by default with Azure Backup' (soft delete), last updated 2026-08-14
sources.note: Relevant text: 'The retention period is 14 days by default. You can extend it up to 180 days'; soft delete is enforced in regions where secure-by-default is in preview or GA, but 'For a Backup vault, in regions other than Australia East, West Central US, and East Asia, you still have the option to disable soft delete from the Azure portal.' Read through a summarizing fetch on 2026-11-14. The scenario's vault is one where soft delete can still be turned off, which is why MUA matters.
